title: Standard of Iron has finally been approved for Steam!
author: standardofiron
selftext:
After spending an unreasonable amount of time staring at formations, pathfinding, tiny soldiers, and increasingly questionable battlefield situations, Standard of Iron finally has an approved Steam page.

It’s an RTS set during an alternate Second Punic War, built around the idea that a battle should actually feel like a war, not couple individual soldiers.

One of the main reasons I ended up writing my own engine was because I wanted thousands of units on screen and simulated at the same time. Large armies can clash across the map while towns grow, resources move around, defenses are built, and AI factions continue doing their own thing.

And the AI isn’t just spawning a pre-designed base.

AI players actually build their own towns, making decisions about where and what to construct, so settlements naturally end up looking different instead of every enemy having the exact same copy-pasted base.

A few of the bigger things in the game:

* Full-scale battles with thousands of units rendered and simulated simultaneously AI-controlled factions that build their own unique towns 
* Formations, infantry, archers, cavalry, elephants and siege weapons 
* Base building, economy, fortifications and sieges  
* The ability to directly control your commander during the battle 
* A custom engine I wrote specifically for this kind of large-scale RTS simulation 
* A heavily data-driven design, units, maps, missions, factions and other content are designed to be changed without rewriting the engine  
* Maps and missions can keep being added or modified as the game develops  
* And the entire project is open source, so you can actually look at the code, break it, fix it, contribute something, or tell me why I did something horribly wrong 😄

I do use AI-assisted tools during development for routine work like refactoring, tests, boilerplate and implementing straightforward systems. I design the systems and architecture, review what goes in, and spend the important part of development actually testing whether any of this is fun.

Steam:  
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5129960/Standard\_of\_Iron/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5129960/Standard_of_Iron/)

Getting the Steam page approved feels like a pretty huge milestone.
